title: Flow-normalized total phosphorus per unit sediment doubled in two Gulf river load estimates from 1981-1996 to 2009-2025
abstract: We compared total phosphorus load per unit suspended sediment in two Gulf river outlets. We used USGS version 3.0 stationary flow-normalized loads for 1981-1996 and 2009-2025. The combined ratio rose from 0.750 to 1.527 mg P per gram of sediment, a factor of 2.036. Mean annual phosphorus load rose by 12.3%, while sediment load fell by 44.9%. Both branches and two normalization methods gave an increase. If every annual source load lies within its marginal 90% bounds, the combined factor is between 1.400 and 2.906. This is a conditional envelope, not a confidence interval; joint source coverage is unknown. Total phosphorus includes dissolved forms, so the ratio does not measure particle composition. Shared source errors and model assumptions limit physical inference. The package includes code, aggregate evidence, a figure, source hashes and an independent calculation check. External raw data stay outside the package.

display.caption: Combined annual total phosphorus-to-sediment load ratios and recent-to-baseline factors. Bars show bounds conditional on simultaneous containment in all source marginal limits. They are not confidence intervals.

citations.reason: Related annual nutrient response test using the same source release. Our endpoint uses sediment and period ratios.
